note_tweet.text:
Managing agents is starting to look like its own job description, and it's showing up fastest at companies too small to have ever written one.

Immad's read is that Grok Bot and ChatGPT Dots are about to do to ops, sales, and support what Claude Code did to engineering, and the startups he's watching aren't doing that work manually anymore, they're managing the agents that do it.

Lay the three live products next to each other and the category's actual shape comes through. Grok Bot, out since August, is a roster of specialist bots that hand work off to each other and can be published into Slack as a shared team resource. ChatGPT Dots, out since late September, is the opposite bet: one persistent assistant that follows you everywhere, built on GPT-6 Astra with memory and over 4,000 connected apps, no multi-bot system at all. Meta Muse took a third path, a personal agent with its own secure VM for passwords and payments and a separate approval agent called Sentinel, and it hit the top of the US app charts within a month of launching.

None of the three has actually solved the trust question yet. Grok Bot's personal bots reportedly share one cloud computer, browser sessions and stored credentials included, so running several of them isn't the security boundary people assume it is. Muse drew complaints almost immediately for reaching into private messages and emails without clear permission, and Amazon banned it outright rather than let an agent shop on its site unsupervised. Adoption is outrunning the governance model by a wide margin.

What strikes me isn't the capability jump, it's how fast the job itself is being redefined underneath people who never opted into the change. Immad's blunt line was that the job stops being doing the thing and becomes training and managing the agent that does the thing. For ops, sales, and support specifically, that's not a future quarter problem. It's already the actual job at the startups he's describing, whether or not the tooling underneath it is ready to be trusted with real customer data.
